round_5.redo_bound: CALLEE_VOTE_MAX_LINES = 32 printed lines of the FIRST decompile; the function is dropped from the ledger before decide(), so nothing is stated, no round pays, and seed/converge have nothing to apply. Chosen from the measured redo profile (per-redo length, ms and whether the body changed) and validated by the redo share: 32 lines keeps kmod at 3.4-4.3% (40 lines 5.7-7.6%, unbounded 13.6-14.5%).
round_5.why_not_an_oracle: Skipping only the redos that change nothing would leave kmod at about +8.5% and crontab at +9.0%: 20 of kmod's 58 redos are wasted but they are 147 of its 571 ms, and crontab's whole cost is one 189-line redo that does change its body.

round_6.what: The flat 32-line refusal on the redo became a budget: the pass may reprint CALLEE_VOTE_BUDGET_PCT (5) percent of the lines the first pass printed, one budget for all three rounds, admitted shortest first (ties to the lower address), and a function printing at most CALLEE_VOTE_MAX_LINES (32) lines is admitted even once that is spent. A function the budget cannot reach is declined for the run (Ledger::decline: own + stated removed, so no later round proposes it and the convergence sweep has nothing to apply).
round_6.why_not_incremental: A redo costs exactly what the first decompile of the same function cost -- median ratio 1.01 over kmod -O2-noinline's 55 redos (range 0.97-1.05) -- so there is no overhead of its own to remove. Of a redo, 12.3% is the flow follow and 58.5% is the action pipeline before the first effective ActionInferTypes (it is inert until ActionStartTypes, which runs in fullloop after a whole mainloop), so 70.8% is work the vote provably cannot change. Re-running 'only type propagation and the emit tier' is not available either: ActionInferTypes sits inside the repeating mainloop and the pools that rewrite ops from the types it decides (ptrarith, ptrsubundo, structoffset0, structsynth) run after it in the same iteration. Reusing that 70.8% means checkpointing the Funcdata where ActionStartTypes first fires and re-entering the action tree at a position -- a pipeline-substrate change (Funcdata deep copy + positional re-entry), PROPOSAL-class, and the one lever that would make an unbounded redo affordable (kmod 10.5% -> about 3%).
round_6.instrument: The redo pass is one call in decompile_callee_first, so its cost is read off a single run (its ms over the run's wall clock) instead of differenced from two whole-binary wall times, which on this box is noisier than the effect (round 5 measured the same kmod build +9.4% by min-of-15 and +2.3% by median). KUNA_CALLEEVOTE_TRACE=1 also prints the pass's deterministic line spend.
